newsitem.title: USA: North Atlantic Tech defaults, lenders to foreclose.
newsitem.headline: North Atlantic Tech defaults, lenders to foreclose.

text.p: North Atlantic Technologies Inc NATTQ.OB said it defaulted on a payment of its line of credit with First Bank N.A., and First Bank intends to foreclose on the assets which secured that loan.
The payment was due June 1, 1997. Those assets comprise all the assets of North Atlantic except its manufacturing facility in St. Paul, Minn., the company said.

This default also is a default under the mortgage on the manufacturing facility. The mortgagee, WDH Investments Co, notified North Atlantic that it also intended to foreclose, thus leaving North Atlantic with no assets.

Because of these events, North Atlantic said it negotiated with First Bank, WDH and Willis Heim, the sole shareholder of WDH, for concessions intended to benefit the employees, customers, stockholders and creditors.
In return for these concessions, North Atlantic agreed to permit the foreclosure actions to occur without contest and without filing for protection under bankruptcy laws.

As part of an overall agreement, WDH has agreed to purchase the assets secured by First Bank in its foreclosure actions and assume the continued operation and substantially all the known liabilities of North Atlantic.

As part of the agreement, about four months following the foreclosure action, WDH will offer to purchase shares of North Atlantic's outstanding preferred and common stock for $1.00 and $0.06 per share, respectively.

"The Board of Directors determined that because of North Atlantic's lack of capital, it has been increasingly difficult to secure orders for its product, and cash flow projections provided to the board demonstrated that North Atlantic could not survive much beyond July of this year, even if the line of credit with First Bank had been extended," said Louis Wagner, chairman of North Atlantic.

"With this agreement in place, we have managed to save something for everyone. Our analysis disclosed that the alternative would have left the stockholders with nothing and would likely have resulted in the loss of the jobs of all of North Atlantic's employees."
Implementation of the agreement is scheduled to occur on July 1, 1997.
North Atlantic makes and markets heat exchangers for the petrochemical and other industries.
